what: Textron builds Cessna and Beechcraft business aircraft, Bell helicopters including the army's next tiltrotor, armoured vehicles and weapons systems, and the Arctic Cat and E-Z-GO vehicles.
customers: Corporate flight departments and wealthy individuals buying business jets, plus the United States military and allied governments.
money: Cessna Citation jets, King Air turboprops and parts
commercial and military helicopters, and the V-280 tiltrotor programme
moat: Certified aircraft designs and an installed fleet that needs parts and service for decades, plus defence programmes awarded once and then flown for a generation.
risks: Business jet orders fall quickly when companies cut spending
The Bell tiltrotor programme is large but its funding is set each year by Congress
A 6.2% net margin: aerospace manufacturing is capital-heavy and slow to scale
opportunities: 14.6 times earnings with $2.0B of cash against only $404M of debt
Analysts see about 25% upside, and revenue grew from $12.4B to $14.8B in four years
Winning the army's Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft gives Bell decades of production
watch: Business jet orders and the backlog, and milestone progress on the tiltrotor programme.
